scenes.text: UPI is getting a fee tomorrow.
But YOU don't pay it.
Shops pay 0.4% on payments above ₹2,000.
Sending money to people: still free.
scenes.sub: Shop payments up to ₹2,000: no fee.

scenes.text: Send this to your family group.

caption:
UPI is getting a fee from 15 October. Here's who actually pays (it's not you).

A 0.4% merchant fee applies to specified UPI payments to shops above ₹2,000, capped at ₹300. Sending money to people stays free, and so do shop payments up to ₹2,000. NPCI says consumers can keep using UPI free.

Source: NPCI FAQ, via SCC Online

One check decides it.
Biometric Aadhaar check is now compulsory.
scenes.sub: For subsidised LPG refills, since 1 October.

scenes.text: 27.43 crore homes have already done it.
scenes.sub: Done once? You need nothing more.

scenes.text: Not sure? Ask the delivery person, the distributor, or your gas app.

caption:
Your subsidised gas cylinder booking needs one thing now: a fingerprint.

From 1 October, biometric Aadhaar authentication is mandatory for subsidised domestic LPG refills. 27.43 crore consumers have already done it. You can do it at delivery, at your distributor, or on your oil company's app.

Source: All India Radio News, 19 Sep 2026

scenes.text: Your parents will get this call.
"This is CBI. You are under digital arrest."
Real agencies never arrest anyone on a video call.
scenes.sub: CBI, police, ED, customs, judges: never.

scenes.text: Hang up. Don't pay. Call 1930.
Send this to them now.

caption:
Your parents will get this call. Make sure they know it's a scam.

Fraudsters pose as CBI, police, customs or ED officers on video calls, claim you're caught in a crime, keep you 'under digital arrest' on camera and demand money. The government's cyber crime centre (I4C) says real agencies never arrest anyone on a video call.

Hang up. Don't pay. Report on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in.

Source: I4C advisory, via PTI

caption:
Is WhatsApp charging you for messages? No.

Meta's new India pricing applies to the WhatsApp Business Platform, which companies use for bulk order and delivery messages: 1,000 free support replies a month per number, then ₹0.115 per message plus GST. The normal WhatsApp app and the WhatsApp Business app aren't affected.

Source: Meta pricing change, via Sunday Guardian, 1 Oct 2026
